event.text: First I'm checking memory for earlier lessons about this lot's supplier or stores.

call.name: recall_memory
cypher:
MATCH (s:Supplier)-[:SUPPLIED]->(l:Lot {code: $lot})
OPTIONAL MATCH (l)-[:USED_IN|REWORKED_INTO|PRODUCED*1..6]->(pl:ProductLot)
WITH s, collect(DISTINCT pl.sku) AS skus
WITH s, [(p:Product)-[:SHIPPED_UNTRACKED]->(a:Store) WHERE p.sku IN skus | a.id]
       + [(q:ProductLot)-[:SHIPPED_TO]->(b:Store) WHERE q.sku IN skus | b.id] AS stores
MATCH (m:Memory)-[:ABOUT]->(x)
WHERE m.lot <> $lot AND (x = s OR (x:Store AND x.id IN stores))
RETURN m.lot AS from_lot, m.at AS at, labels(x)[0] AS kind, x.id AS about, m.fact AS fact
ORDER BY at DESC, about LIMIT 20

cypher:
MERGE (i:Incident {lot: $lot})
ON CREATE SET i.id = $id, i.reported_at = $at, i.hazard = 'not recorded'
SET i.class = $class, i.depth = $depth, i.rationale = $rationale, i.classified_at = $at
RETURN i.id AS id, i.hazard AS hazard

event.text: Next I'm placing a hold so nothing unshipped leaves, and tracing forward to find affected stores.

call.name: trace_forward
cypher:
MATCH path = (l:Lot {code: $lot})-[:USED_IN|REWORKED_INTO|PRODUCED|SHIPPED_TO*1..8]->(st:Store)
RETURN st.id AS store,
       [n IN nodes(path) | coalesce(n.code, n.id)] AS path,
       [n IN nodes(path) | labels(n)[0]] AS kinds,
       last(relationships(path)).units AS units

call.name: place_hold
call.summary: 2,652 units and 93 kg of raw L-204 held at 5 locations
cypher:
MATCH (l:Lot {code: $lot})-[s:STORED_AT]->(site:Site)
RETURN site.id AS id, site.name AS name, site.city AS city, site.region AS region, s.qty_kg AS qty_kg, l.received_kg AS received_kg

MATCH (:Lot {code: $lot})-[:USED_IN|REWORKED_INTO|PRODUCED*1..6]->(pl:ProductLot)-[h:HELD_AT]->(loc)
WITH DISTINCT pl, h, loc
MATCH (pl)-[:OF]->(p:Product)
RETURN pl.id AS product_lot, p.name AS product, labels(loc)[0] AS kind, loc.id AS id, loc.name AS name,
       loc.city AS city, loc.region AS region, h.units AS units
ORDER BY kind, id, product_lot

MATCH (:Lot {code: $lot})-[:USED_IN|REWORKED_INTO|PRODUCED*1..6]->(:ProductLot)-[h:HELD_AT]->()
SET h.held_for = $lot, h.held_at = $at

event.text: Now I'm ranking chokepoints and checking for coverage gaps.

call.name: rank_chokepoints
call.summary: B-03 is the chokepoint: betweenness 175, 16 stores downstream
cypher:
CALL algo.betweenness({nodeLabels: ['Lot', 'Batch', 'ProductLot', 'Store'], relationshipTypes: ['USED_IN', 'REWORKED_INTO', 'PRODUCED', 'SHIPPED_TO'], samplingSize: 1000, samplingSeed: 7})
YIELD node, score
WITH node, score WHERE score > 0 AND (node:Batch OR node:ProductLot)
MATCH (:Lot {code: $lot})-[:USED_IN|REWORKED_INTO|PRODUCED*1..6]->(node)
WITH DISTINCT node, score
OPTIONAL MATCH (node)-[:REWORKED_INTO|PRODUCED|SHIPPED_TO*1..6]->(st:Store)
RETURN labels(node)[0] AS kind, node.id AS id, score, count(DISTINCT st) AS stores
ORDER BY score DESC, id LIMIT 5

call.name: coverage_gaps
call.summary: 2 stores got Garden Vegetable Stew with no lot code on the delivery record

WHERE p.sku IN skus

result.summary: I've proposed Class I, consumer-level for L-204, because Listeria in chilled ready-to-eat food is a serious risk; memory says this lot explains all 6 cases in outbreak OB-2026-10. The hold covers 93 kg of unused carrot at Northfield Plant 2 and 2,652 unshipped units at three distribution centres and two plants. The lot reached 31 stores through batches B-03, B-05, B-07 and B-09, and B-03 is the chokepoint: its leftovers were reused in B-09 (product lot TLC-09A), so that rework step is the place to fix. I added ST-013 and ST-021 because each got Garden Vegetable Stew with no lot code recorded, so they can't be proven safe; nothing in memory was about these two stores. Checking backward, none of the 8 product lots held by the 38 cleared stores contains L-204. That's 33 stores to recall instead of 71 for a blanket recall, with 38 cleared and 2,256 units to pull, and the class, the hold release and the 33 draft notices all wait for the coordinator's approval.
